title: Template Zero: clone, add your key, it works
pitch: You build an AI project template that anyone can clone and have running in ten minutes: keys kept out of the code, versions pinned, Docker so the computer doesn't matter, and a checker that confirms nothing is missing before it starts. This is the skeleton you'll reuse in every project you build from here on, and the one you show off when someone asks if you know how to set up an environment.
outcome: An eight-file folder, saved in Git, that someone else clones on their computer and starts with a single command (docker compose up --build) without asking you anything. Inside is a real app that summarizes text using the Anthropic API and tells you how much each call cost, and a comprobar.py script that stops with a clear message if a key, a package, or a version is missing or mismatched.
requires: Python 3.10 or higher. Check with: python --version. If you don't have it, it's a free download from python.org (choose 3.12).
Docker Desktop installed and open. Free for personal use, education, and small businesses; from 250 employees or $10M in revenue it costs about $9 per user per month.
An account at console.anthropic.com with balance. The API has no free plan: it's pay-per-use. Loading $5 is plenty, this entire project doesn't reach $0.10.
A text editor. VS Code is free and works well.
Knowing how to open a terminal and move between folders with cd.

structure.what: The list of keys and settings that are needed, without the real values. It's the map that whoever clones the project reads to know what to fill in. This file does get pushed to Git.
The list of what Git has to ignore. The line that matters is the first: .env. Without it, some day you push your key without meaning to.
Each package with its exact version number. This is what makes the project behave the same today, six months from now, and on someone else's laptop.
The traffic light. Checks the Python version, environment variables, packages, write permissions, and, if you ask it to, the API itself. If something fails, it says so and won't let you start.
The example app: summarizes a text with the Anthropic API, saves the result to disk, and tells you how many tokens it used and what it cost.
The recipe for the box: what Python, what packages, what files go in, and what runs on startup. Notice what's not in it: the .env.
The start button. Turns half a dozen Docker options nobody remembers into a single command.
Instructions for whoever arrives new. Without this the template isn't clonable: it's yours and only yours.

steps.title: The folder, the history, and the package box
steps.why: Before writing a line of code you need three things: a folder, a change history, and an isolated place to install packages. That last one is what most people skip, and it's what keeps next week's project from breaking this week's.
steps.code:
# 1. Create the project folder and go into it.
mkdir plantilla-ia
cd plantilla-ia

# 2. Start Git. Git is the project's logbook: it saves every
#    change and lets you go back. Without it there's no clonable project.
git init

# 3. Create a "virtual environment": a box of packages that only exists
#    inside this folder. Without this, everything you install mixes
#    with the rest of your computer and you end up with clashing versions.
python -m venv .venv

# 4. Activate it. This line is for Windows with PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# 4-bis. If you're on Mac or Linux, delete the line above and use this:
# source .venv/bin/activate

# 5. Check you're inside the box. The path that comes out has to
#    go through .venv. If it shows the system Python's path, it's not activated.
python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"
steps.expected: git init answers something like "Initialized empty Git repository". After activating the environment, (.venv) appears at the start of the terminal line. And the last command prints a long path ending in .venv/Scripts/python.exe on Windows, or .venv/bin/python on Mac and Linux.
steps.trouble: On Windows, Activate.ps1 usually gives "running scripts is disabled on this system". Fix it by running once: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned, and answering Y. If it says "python" doesn't exist, try py -3 on Windows or python3 on Mac.

steps.title: The two files that protect your key
steps.why: Here you decide what gets shared and what doesn't, and that decision follows you into every project you build afterward. .gitignore is the wall. .env.example is the door with a sign saying which key is needed, without leaving the key in the lock.
steps.code:
# =====================================================================
# FILE 1 of 2 -> create a file named exactly: .gitignore
# (yes, it starts with a dot and has no extension)
# =====================================================================

# .env carries your key. It must NEVER leave your computer.
.env

# The package box. It weighs hundreds of megabytes and regenerates itself.
.venv/
venv/

# Junk Python generates while running.
__pycache__/
*.pyc

# The results the app produces. Not code.
salidas/

# Operating system junk.
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db


# =====================================================================
# FILE 2 of 2 -> create a file named exactly: .env.example
# This one DOES get pushed. It's the map: it says what keys are needed, without the values.
# =====================================================================

# Your Anthropic API key. Get it at console.anthropic.com,
# under API Keys. Always starts with sk-ant-
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=CHANGE_paste_your_key_here

# Which model you use. claude-haiku-4-5 is the cheap and fast one.
MODELO=claude-haiku-4-5

# Response limit, measured in tokens. A token is a chunk of a word:
# 400 tokens is about 300 words in English.
LIMITE_RESPUESTA=400

# Name that shows up in the on-screen messages.
NOMBRE_PROYECTO=Summarizer


# =====================================================================
# AND NOW, IN THE TERMINAL: create your real .env by copying the example.
# =====================================================================
cp .env.example .env

# Open .env in the editor and replace CHANGE_paste_your_key_here with your key.
# WARNING: if you ever push .env to GitHub, the key stays in the
# history forever. Deleting the commit does NOT save it. The only fix
# is to go to console.anthropic.com and revoke that key. That's irreversible:
# anything using it stops working instantly.
steps.expected: You now have three new files: .gitignore, .env.example, and .env. If you run git status, Git lists .gitignore and .env.example as new files, and .env doesn't show up anywhere. If .env appears in that list, .gitignore is written wrong or is in the wrong folder.
steps.trouble: Windows saving the file as ".gitignore.txt" without telling you. You'll see it by running ls: the .txt extension shows up tacked on the end. The safe way is to create the files from VS Code, with File > New File, typing the full name with the dot in front.

steps.title: Pin the versions
steps.why: Without pinned versions, "pip install anthropic" today and six months from now installs different things, and a project that worked stops working without you having touched a single line. Pinning versions is what turns "it works on my machine" into "it works".
steps.code:
# Make sure the virtual environment is still active: (.venv) has to show
# at the start of the terminal line. If not, go back to step 1.

# 1. Install the two pieces this project needs.
#    anthropic     = the official package for talking to the Claude API
#    python-dotenv = the one that reads the .env file and loads keys into memory
pip install anthropic python-dotenv

# 2. Freeze what's installed. "pip freeze" spits out the exact list of
#    everything in the box, with its version number. It includes
#    dependencies of dependencies, which is exactly what you want: if httpx
#    ships a new version next week, your project doesn't notice.
pip freeze > requirements.txt

# 3. Look at it. Each line is "package==version". That's pinning versions.
cat requirements.txt

# 4. Golden rule: every time you install something new, freeze again.
#    pip install <whatever> && pip freeze > requirements.txt
#    Forget it and your teammate clones the project and is missing a package.
steps.expected: requirements.txt exists and has between 12 and 18 lines, each shaped package==number. You'll see anthropic and python-dotenv, plus dependencies of dependencies: httpx, pydantic, anyio, certifi, sniffio, and a few more. The exact numbers will differ from a teammate's if you install on different dates, and that's fine: what matters is that they're pinned.
steps.trouble: If requirements.txt comes out almost empty, or full of odd packages you didn't install, the virtual environment wasn't active and you froze the system Python instead. Delete it, activate .venv (you have to see (.venv) at the start of the line), and repeat pip install and pip freeze.

steps.title: The traffic light: comprobar.py
steps.why: This is the heart of the project and what sets it apart from any random folder. Without a checker, you find out something's missing halfway through the run, with an error in English from a library you didn't write. With a checker, you find out in the first second, in plain language, with the exact command to fix it.
steps.code:
"""
comprobar.py  -  The project's traffic light.

Goes through every piece needed to start, one by one. If something's
missing, it says so and tells you how to fix it. It doesn't run anything else.

Usage:
    python comprobar.py         Local checks. Free, 1 second.
    python comprobar.py --api   Also makes a real call. Costs ~$0.0001.
"""

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from importlib.metadata import version, PackageNotFoundError

# Folder where this file lives. That way it works no matter where you call it from.
RAIZ = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# We track what's failing here, to give the verdict at the end.
FALLOS = []

# Note: the printed messages avoid accented characters on purpose. Some
# Windows terminals still choke printing accents, and a checker that
# crashes while checking is no use to anyone.


def titulo(texto):
    print("")
    print(texto)
    print("-" * len(texto))


def ok(texto):
    print("  [OK]    " + texto)


def mal(texto, arreglo):
    print("  [FAIL] " + texto)
    print("          Fix: " + arreglo)
    FALLOS.append(texto)


def aviso(texto):
    print("  [NOTE]  " + texto)


def tapar(nombre, valor):
    """Never print a whole key. Not even on your own screen: screenshots
    get shared and logs get saved."""
    secreto = "KEY" in nombre or "SECRET" in nombre or "PASSWORD" in nombre
    if secreto:
        return valor[:10] + "... (" + str(len(valor)) + " characters)"
    return valor


def leer_pares(ruta):
    """Turns a KEY=value style file into a Python dictionary."""
    pares = {}
    if not ruta.exists():
        return pares
    for linea in ruta.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        linea = linea.strip()
        if not linea or linea.startswith("#") or "=" not in linea:
            continue
        nombre, valor = linea.split("=", 1)
        pares[nombre.strip()] = valor.strip()
    return pares


def cargar_env():
    """Loads whatever's in .env into memory. If there's no .env, that's fine:
    inside Docker the variables are already set from outside."""
    try:
        from dotenv import load_dotenv
    except ImportError:
        return
    load_dotenv(RAIZ / ".env")


def paso_python():
    titulo("1. Python version")
    v = sys.version_info
    actual = "%d.%d.%d" % (v.major, v.minor, v.micro)
    if (v.major, v.minor) >= (3, 10):
        ok("Python " + actual)
    else:
        mal("Python " + actual + " is too old",
            "Install Python 3.12 from python.org and recreate .venv")


def paso_variables():
    titulo("2. Keys and environment variables")
    ejemplo = leer_pares(RAIZ / ".env.example")
    if not ejemplo:
        mal("Can't find .env.example or it's empty",
            "Go back to step 2 and create the .env.example file")
        return

    if (RAIZ / ".env").exists():
        ok("The .env file exists")
    else:
        aviso("No .env file. Only fine if the variables come from outside (Docker)")

    # The trick: the list of required variables comes from .env.example.
    # Add a new variable to the example tomorrow and the checker already requires it.
    for nombre in ejemplo:
        valor = os.environ.get(nombre, "")
        if not valor:
            mal("Missing variable " + nombre,
                "Open .env and add the line " + nombre + "=<your value>")
        elif valor.startswith("CHANGE"):
            mal("Variable " + nombre + " still has the placeholder text",
                "Open .env and put the real value in " + nombre)
        else:
            ok(nombre + " = " + tapar(nombre, valor))

    # One last check on the key: all Anthropic keys start the same way.
    # This catches the most common mistake of all: pasting it halfway.
    clave = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "")
    if clave and not clave.startswith("CHANGE") and not clave.startswith("sk-ant-"):
        mal("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY doesn't start with 'sk-ant-'",
            "You copied it halfway or a space snuck in. Copy it whole again")


def paso_paquetes():
    titulo("3. Packages with pinned versions")
    ruta = RAIZ / "requirements.txt"
    if not ruta.exists():
        mal("Can't find requirements.txt", "Run: pip freeze > requirements.txt")
        return

    correctos = []
    revisados = 0
    for linea in ruta.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        linea = linea.strip()
        if not linea or linea.startswith("#") or "==" not in linea:
            continue
        paquete, pedida = linea.split("==", 1)
        paquete = paquete.strip()
        pedida = pedida.strip()
        revisados += 1
        try:
            puesta = version(paquete)
        except PackageNotFoundError:
            mal("Missing package " + paquete + " " + pedida,
                "Run: pip install -r requirements.txt")
            continue
        if puesta != pedida:
            mal(paquete + ": you have " + puesta + " and the project needs " + pedida,
                "Run: pip install -r requirements.txt")
        else:
            correctos.append(paquete + " " + puesta)

    if revisados == 0:
        mal("requirements.txt doesn't pin any version (no == found)",
            "Run: pip freeze > requirements.txt")
    elif correctos:
        muestra = ", ".join(correctos[:3])
        if len(correctos) > 3:
            muestra = muestra + ", and " + str(len(correctos) - 3) + " more"
        ok(str(len(correctos)) + " packages with the exact version: " + muestra)


def paso_salidas():
    titulo("4. Output folder")
    carpeta = RAIZ / "salidas"
    try:
        carpeta.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        prueba = carpeta / ".prueba_escritura"
        prueba.write_text("ok", encoding="utf-8")
        prueba.unlink()
        ok("Can write to " + str(carpeta))
    except Exception as error:
        mal("Can't write to " + str(carpeta) + " -> " + str(error),
            "On Mac or Linux: chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) salidas")


def paso_api():
    titulo("5. Real API call")
    if "--api" not in sys.argv:
        aviso("Skipped. Run 'python comprobar.py --api' to test it for real")
        return

    try:
        import anthropic
    except ImportError:
        mal("The anthropic package isn't installed",
            "Run: pip install -r requirements.txt")
        return

    clave = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "")
    modelo = os.environ.get("MODELO", "claude-haiku-4-5")
    if not clave:
        mal("No key, no call", "Fill in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env")
        return

    try:
        cliente = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=clave)
        respuesta = cliente.messages.create(
            model=modelo,
            max_tokens=10,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply only with the word: pong"}],
        )
        ok("Model " + modelo + " replies: " + respuesta.content[0].text.strip())
        ok("Cost of this test: " + str(respuesta.usage.input_tokens)
           + " input tokens and " + str(respuesta.usage.output_tokens) + " output tokens")
    except anthropic.AuthenticationError:
        mal("The API rejects your key (error 401)",
            "It's wrong, expired, or revoked. Generate a new one at console.anthropic.com")
    except anthropic.NotFoundError:
        mal("Model '" + modelo + "' doesn't exist or you don't have access",
            "Check the MODELO value in your .env")
    except Exception as error:
        mal("The call failed: " + type(error).__name__ + " -> " + str(error),
            "Check your internet connection and your balance at console.anthropic.com")


def main():
    print("Checking the project at: " + str(RAIZ))
    cargar_env()
    paso_python()
    paso_variables()
    paso_paquetes()
    paso_salidas()
    paso_api()

    print("")
    if FALLOS:
        print("RESULT: " + str(len(FALLOS)) + " problem(s). The project is NOT ready.")
        print("Fix what's above and run again: python comprobar.py")
        # Exiting with code 1 is the universal signal for "something went wrong".
        # Docker and CI servers understand it and stop.
        sys.exit(1)

    print("RESULT: everything's fine. Start with: python app.py")
    sys.exit(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.expected: The file gets created and VS Code doesn't underline anything in red. You don't run it yet: that's step 6. Notice one detail: the list of required variables isn't hardcoded, it's read from .env.example. Add a variable to the example tomorrow and the checker already requires it on its own.
steps.trouble: Indentation errors from copy-pasting. Python counts left-margin spaces: each level is 4 and they all have to line up. If you get IndentationError or "unexpected indent", paste the whole file at once instead of piece by piece, which is when things get misaligned.

steps.title: The example app: app.py
steps.why: An empty template can't be tested. This app is small but does the same thing any AI project you build afterward will do: reads config from the environment, calls a model, saves the result to disk, and tells you what it cost.
steps.code:
"""
app.py  -  Summarizes a text with the Anthropic API.

Usage:
    python app.py                  Summarizes the example text.
    python app.py minutes.txt      Summarizes the file you pass it.

All configuration comes from environment variables. There isn't a single
key written in this file. That's the rule that never gets broken.
"""

import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv
import anthropic

RAIZ = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# Loads .env if it exists. Inside Docker it doesn't exist, but the
# variables are already set from outside and this line simply does nothing.
load_dotenv(RAIZ / ".env")

# Prices for claude-haiku-4-5 per million tokens, in dollars.
# If you switch models in .env, change these two numbers too.
PRECIO_ENTRADA = 1.00
PRECIO_SALIDA = 5.00

TEXTO_EJEMPLO = (
    "Minutes of the March 12th meeting. Attending: Marta Ruiz (management), "
    "Javier Peña (operations), and Lucia Ferrer (finance). It's approved "
    "to raise the logistics budget from 48,000 to 61,000 euros to cover "
    "the growth in online-channel orders, which have grown 34% versus "
    "the previous quarter. Javier warns that the Getafe warehouse is "
    "at 91% capacity and proposes renting an extra 400 square meters in "
    "Pinto for 2,300 euros a month. Lucia asks for an analysis of three "
    "suppliers before signing. It's decided to postpone the decision to "
    "March 26th. Marta assigns the analysis to Javier and sets the deadline "
    "at March 22nd. No other line item changes."
)


def leer_texto():
    """If you pass it a file via the terminal, it reads that. If not, uses the example."""
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        ruta = Path(sys.argv[1])
        if not ruta.exists():
            print("File doesn't exist: " + str(ruta))
            sys.exit(1)
        return ruta.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    return TEXTO_EJEMPLO


def main():
    # The three lines that matter: none of this is hardcoded in the code.
    clave = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
    modelo = os.environ.get("MODELO", "claude-haiku-4-5")
    limite = int(os.environ.get("LIMITE_RESPUESTA", "400"))
    nombre = os.environ.get("NOMBRE_PROYECTO", "Summarizer")

    if not clave:
        print("Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Run first: python comprobar.py")
        sys.exit(1)

    texto = leer_texto()
    print("[" + nombre + "] Summarizing " + str(len(texto)) + " characters with " + modelo)

    cliente = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=clave)
    respuesta = cliente.messages.create(
        model=modelo,
        max_tokens=limite,
        # The "system" is the permanent instruction: who you are and how you write.
        system=(
            "You are an editor. Summarize in at most 5 bullet points, "
            "in plain, direct English, no flourishes. "
            "Keep every figure, name, and date from the original."
        ),
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this text:\n\n" + texto}],
    )

    resumen = respuesta.content[0].text
    print("")
    print(resumen)
    print("")

    # Saves the result with the date and time in the filename, so you
    # don't overwrite the previous summary every time you run the app.
    carpeta = RAIZ / "salidas"
    carpeta.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    sello = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    destino = carpeta / ("summary-" + sello + ".md")
    destino.write_text(resumen, encoding="utf-8")

    entrada = respuesta.usage.input_tokens
    salida = respuesta.usage.output_tokens
    coste = entrada / 1_000_000 * PRECIO_ENTRADA + salida / 1_000_000 * PRECIO_SALIDA

    print("Saved to: " + str(destino))
    print("Tokens: " + str(entrada) + " input, " + str(salida) + " output")
    print("Approximate cost: " + format(coste, ".5f") + " USD")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
steps.expected: The file gets created. Go over the four config lines inside main(): all of them start with os.environ.get. In all of app.py there's no key written, no fixed model name that can't be changed from .env.
steps.trouble: When you run it in the next step, the typical error is "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named dotenv". It means the virtual environment isn't active or you didn't install the packages. Activate it and run: pip install -r requirements.txt

steps.title: Test it on your computer
steps.why: You won't know if it works until you run it. And notice the order: first what's free, then what costs money. That habit will save you scares the day you work with expensive models and long calls.
steps.code:
# 1. The traffic light, without spending a cent. Takes one second.
python comprobar.py

# 2. If it says "everything's fine", try the real call.
#    This test spends about 20 tokens: less than $0.0001.
python comprobar.py --api

# 3. Now the app. It summarizes the example minutes built into it.
python app.py

# 4. Look at the file it left in the salidas folder.
ls salidas

# 5. Try it with your own text. Create any .txt file and pass it in.
#    python app.py my-text.txt

# 6. And now break something on purpose, to watch the checker work.
#    Open .env, delete the value of MODELO (leave MODELO=) and run:
#    python comprobar.py
#    It has to show [FAIL] and stop before reaching the API. Then fix it.
steps.expected: comprobar.py prints five numbered blocks, each with its [OK]s, and finishes with "RESULT: everything's fine". With --api it adds a line saying the model replies "pong" and how many tokens it used. app.py prints the minutes summarized into 5 bullet points, says where it saved the file, and ends with something like "Approximate cost: 0.00042 USD".
steps.trouble: The most common failure is "[FAIL] The API rejects your key (error 401)". It's almost always a trailing space or a dropped character from copying the key. Open .env, delete the whole line, and paste the key again: right after the equals sign, no spaces, no quotes.

steps.title: Put it all in a box: the Dockerfile
steps.why: The virtual environment fixes the packages, but it doesn't fix the system. If your teammate has Python 3.9, or is missing an OS-level library, your project won't start on their machine. Docker packs the system, the Python version, and the packages into a sealed box that behaves the same everywhere.
steps.code:
# FILE -> create a file named exactly: Dockerfile (no extension)

# The base image: Python 3.12 on a trimmed-down Debian. "slim" means
# no extras, about 150 MB instead of 1 GB. Notice the 3.12: that's also
# pinning a version. If you put "python:latest", tomorrow it isn't the same.
FROM python:3.12-slim

# From here on, everything that happens inside the box happens in /app.
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the versions file FIRST, only. Docker caches the result of
# each line. If requirements.txt doesn't change, it skips the whole install
# and the build goes from 40 seconds to 2.
COPY requirements.txt .

# --no-cache-dir: doesn't keep the downloaded packages. The image is smaller.
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Now the code, which is what you change ten times a day.
# Notice what's NOT here: .env. Keys never go into the image.
# An image gets pushed to a registry and seen by a lot more people than you'd think.
COPY comprobar.py app.py .env.example ./

# Don't run as root inside the container. If something gets in, it does less harm.
RUN useradd --create-home student && chown -R student:student /app
USER student

# On startup: the traffic light first. If comprobar.py exits with an error, the && stops it
# and app.py never runs. The container dies telling you what was missing.
CMD ["sh", "-c", "python comprobar.py && python app.py"]

# Warning: when building, Docker sends the whole folder to the engine, .venv
# included if it's there, and that's hundreds of megabytes and a lot of waiting. It's
# fixed with a .dockerignore file. That's why the final test is done on a clean clone,
# which doesn't have .venv inside it.
steps.expected: The Dockerfile exists in the project folder. You don't build anything yet, that comes in step 9. What you can do is reread the order of the lines: first requirements.txt, then pip install, and the code last. That order is what makes rebuilding take 3 seconds instead of 2 minutes.
steps.trouble: Saving it as "Dockerfile.txt" or as lowercase "dockerfile". It has to be named Dockerfile, capital D, no extension at all. If not, Docker can't find it and throws "failed to read dockerfile: open Dockerfile: no such file or directory".

steps.title: A single command to start
steps.why: Without this file, starting the project is four lines of docker run with options nobody memorizes. With it, it's one command. And those options stay written down and saved in Git, not in the head of whoever set it up and then left the company.
steps.code:
# FILE -> create a file named exactly: docker-compose.yml
# This file stores everything you'd otherwise have to type by hand with "docker run".
# From here on, starting the project is one command, always the same one.

services:
  resumidor:
    # Builds the image using the Dockerfile in this same folder.
    build: .

    # Fixed container name, to find it quickly with "docker ps".
    container_name: resumidor

    # This is where the keys come in: they're read from your .env and injected
    # as environment variables on startup. They're not in the image, they're
    # outside it. If you change the key tomorrow, you don't rebuild anything:
    # you just restart.
    env_file:
      - .env

    # Links your computer's salidas folder to the one inside the box.
    # Without this, you delete the container and the summaries go with it.
    volumes:
      - ./salidas:/app/salidas

    # Don't restart on its own. This is a task that starts, does its job,
    # and finishes, not a server that has to stay alive.
    restart: "no"
steps.expected: The docker-compose.yml file exists. You can validate it without starting anything with: docker compose config. If the YAML is written correctly, it prints back the full configuration, with paths already resolved.
steps.trouble: YAML is picky about spaces and doesn't allow tabs. If it says "yaml: line 4: found character that cannot start any token", there's a tab where there should be spaces. In VS Code you can see it by turning on View > Render Whitespace, and fix it by removing the tab and typing spaces.

steps.title: The README and the trial by fire
steps.why: Everything above could only work on your computer and you'd never know. Cloning the project into a fresh folder and starting it with Docker is the only test that really counts: if it works there, it's reproducible. And the README is what keeps the newcomer from having to ask you anything.
steps.code:
# FIRST THE README. On Mac, Linux, or Git Bash, paste this as-is and it
# creates itself. In PowerShell, create README.md in the editor and paste
# what's between the first FIN line and the last.

cat > README.md <<'FIN'
# AI Template - Summarizer

Reproducible project template. Clone, add your key, it works.

## What you need
- Docker Desktop. With this you don't need anything else.
- Or Python 3.10 or higher, if you want to run it without Docker.
- An Anthropic API key: console.anthropic.com -> API Keys.

## Starting with Docker (recommended)

    cp .env.example .env
    # open .env and paste your key into ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    mkdir salidas
    docker compose up --build

## Starting without Docker

    python -m venv .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
    pip install -r requirements.txt
    cp .env.example .env
    # open .env and paste your key
    python comprobar.py
    python app.py

## This template's three rules
1. .env never gets pushed. It's in .gitignore. .env.example does get pushed.
2. Versions are pinned in requirements.txt. If you install something new,
   run again: pip freeze > requirements.txt
3. If comprobar.py says FAIL, don't continue. Fix that first.

## Cost
Each summary costs under $0.01 with claude-haiku-4-5. The Anthropic API
has no free plan: load $5 and you get thousands of tests like this one.
See your actual spend at console.anthropic.com.
FIN


# NOW THE TRIAL BY FIRE. This is where you see whether the template is truly reproducible.

# 1. Save everything to Git.
git add .
git status
#    Look at the list carefully: .env must NOT appear. If it does, your
#    .gitignore is written wrong or in the wrong place. Stop and fix it.
git commit -m "Reproducible template: env, pinned versions, Docker, and checker"

# 2. Clone the project into a fresh folder, like a new teammate would.
cd ..
git clone plantilla-ia prueba-limpia
cd prueba-limpia

# 3. Look at what's there. No .env, no .venv, no salidas.
#    That's exactly what was supposed to happen.
ls -a

# 4. Add the key. This is done by hand on each machine, always. It's the only
#    thing that doesn't travel with the project, and that's why the project is safe to share.
cp ../plantilla-ia/.env .env
mkdir salidas

# 5. Start it. Docker builds the image, passes the traffic light, and summarizes.
#    The first time takes 1-2 minutes because it downloads Python. After that, 3 seconds.
docker compose up --build

# 6. Clean up the stopped container when you're done.
docker compose down

# WATCH OUT for these two commands, which you should NOT run right now:
#   docker compose down -v      deletes the volumes. Data is lost. Irreversible.
#   docker system prune -a      deletes ALL images on your computer, not just this
#                               project's. Getting them back means downloading everything again.
steps.expected: git status doesn't mention .env anywhere. The clone shows up without .env, without .venv, and without salidas: you see it with ls -a, and that's exactly what was supposed to happen. And docker compose up --build ends up printing, from inside the container, the five blocks with [OK], the summarized minutes, and the cost. The first build takes 1 or 2 minutes because it downloads Python; the next ones, seconds.
steps.trouble: If it says "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon", Docker Desktop isn't open: open it and wait for the whale icon to stop moving. If it says "container name /resumidor is already in use", there's an old stopped container with that name: run docker rm resumidor and try again.

checks: You run git status and .env doesn't show up anywhere. If it does, your key is one commit away from staying in the history forever.
You search for the text sk-ant- inside app.py and comprobar.py and nothing comes up. No key written in the code, not one.

You empty a variable in .env (for example leave MODELO= with nothing) and comprobar.py fails with a [FAIL] that names the variable and says how to fix it, without ever calling the API or spending a cent.
You uninstall a package by hand (pip uninstall python-dotenv) and comprobar.py catches it and gives the exact command to fix it.
Every line in requirements.txt has a ==. Not a single >= and no loose package without a version number.
You clone the project into a new folder, copy over only the .env by hand, and docker compose up --build gets it running without you touching a single line of code.
extend: Add a .dockerignore file with .venv/, .git/, salidas/, and __pycache__/ inside. Rebuild the image and compare how long it takes: "transferring context" goes from hundreds of megabytes to a few kilobytes.

Add a new variable to .env.example, for example IDIOMA_SALIDA=es, and don't touch comprobar.py. Run the checker: it already requires the new variable on its own, because the list comes from .env.example itself. Then actually use it in app.py's system prompt to change the summary's language.

Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that on every push builds the environment, installs requirements.txt, and runs comprobar.py without --api. That way, if someone pushes the project with an outdated version, the warning fires before it reaches production. One thing to watch: on GitHub's server there's no .env file, so you have to put the variables in as repository secrets and pass them to the step with env.
defend: Why not just leave the key written in the code? Because the code gets pushed, shared, and copied, and the key would go with it. With an Anthropic API key, anyone can spend your balance. Pulling it out into .env gives you three things: you can share the code without worry, each machine (your laptop, the server, a teammate's computer) uses a different key without touching a line, and if one leaks you revoke only that one. And if a .env ever does sneak into Git, the fix isn't deleting the commit: it's going to the console and revoking the key, because the history is already scattered out there.

What's the point of Docker if the project already works on your computer? Because "it works on my computer" isn't a deliverable. Docker packs the operating system, the Python version, and the packages into the same box, so what starts on my laptop starts the same way on the server. And for the newcomer the difference is obvious: without Docker they have to install Python, create the virtual environment, install dependencies, and cross their fingers; with Docker they type docker compose up --build and that's it.

What does comprobar.py add, if the app already fails on its own when something's wrong? It adds the timing and the message. Without it, the app crashes halfway through with an error from some library nobody understands, sometimes after already spending money on the API. comprobar.py fails before spending anything, says exactly what's missing, and gives the command to fix it. And it exits with code 1, which is the signal Docker and CI systems understand: that's why the container won't start the app if the traffic light is red.
